title.en: Hormones and Peptides for Skin

summary.en: Designed toward future CME accreditation, this post-graduate clinical course prepares aesthetic and dermatologic clinicians to appraise the endocrine physiology of skin, differentiate pathognomonic endocrine cutaneous signs from isolated cosmetic presentations, evaluate the GRADE evidence and pharmacodynamics of cutaneous peptides and incretin therapies, and navigate regulatory and liability boundaries without promoting unapproved dosing protocols or commercial bias.

client.productContext: Skin edition of the Hormonaly peptide master course; commissioned by SEASON Aesthetic Conferences (Perceptors.ai partnership) and built without waiting for their reviewer.

personas: dermatologist, aesthetic physician or plastic surgeon evaluating hormone and peptide claims for skin
nurse practitioner or physician associate who prescribes or counsels in aesthetic, dermatology or primary care
registered nurse, aesthetic nurse or injector who delivers treatments and fields patient questions
other licensed providers (pharmacists, naturopathic doctors, allied aesthetic professionals) who advise on skin products and referrals

professionalScope.en: Continuing professional education for licensed clinicians and allied providers. Every learner gets the same evidence, regulatory status and safety content; what each may do with it — prescribe, recommend, administer, or refer — follows their own licence and scope, and the course adapts its application layer to that (see metadata.variants). It informs clinical reasoning; it is not a protocol, contains no dosing, and does not replace specialist input, formal guidelines or individual judgment.

disclaimers.en: Educational content for clinicians. It does not prescribe, and it never restates an evidence grade above what the source assigns to the specific indication.
Regulatory statements name their jurisdiction. US compounding examples (FDA 503A/503B) do not describe UK or EU status.
Designed toward future CME accreditation. No CME or CE credit is currently offered.

claims.text: GHK is an endogenous human plasma tripeptide first described in 1973; GHK-Cu is its copper complex.
claims.reviewNote: history; uncontested · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Proposed mechanism: GHK-Cu modulates copper delivery to enzymes including superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and activates wound-healing and antioxidant gene-expression programmes — a mechanistic claim resting on reviews by the peptide's originator.
claims.reviewNote: teach as mechanism with the conflict of interest visible · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small-trial: one PubMed-indexed randomized trial (post-laser wound healing, 2006) and manufacturer-sponsored cosmetic trials that are not indexed; the guides rate the cosmetic indication GRADE C.
claims.reviewNote: grade C per both guides; Omar to confirm · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Injectable GHK-Cu has no randomized human trials; use rests on anecdote, and injection-site pain and rash are common.
claims.reviewNote: safety statement is the guides' clinical observation; Li 2016 is mechanistic support only · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Whether topical GHK-Cu reaches the dermis in meaningful amounts is unsettled; penetration data are in vitro and measurement-dependent.
claims.reviewNote: · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: US status (as of May 14, 2026): GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes sits in FDA's 503A Category 1 (under evaluation) after its nomination was withdrawn on April 22, 2026 and partially reinstated; FDA intends to consult the PCAC on it before the end of February 2027. Category 1 is an enforcement posture, not approval; the injectable route has no such standing.
claims.reviewNote: more precise than either guide's 'Category 1 (non-injectable)'; date-stamp it in the lesson · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) improved photoaging measures in a 12-week randomized trial funded by the manufacturer; the Matrixyl 3000 blend rests on the maker's technical dossier, which is not indexed.
claims.reviewNote: guide grade D; note sponsorship explicitly · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3/-8) mimics the N-terminus of SNAP-25; randomized placebo-controlled trials report modest wrinkle improvement, but delivery to the neuromuscular junction at cosmetic concentrations is considered implausible — the effect, if real, is not a botulinum substitute.
claims.reviewNote: PPG-Aug marks 'Wang Y et al.' as not indexed — the 2013 Am J Clin Dermatol RCT is indexed (PMID 23417317); report to the author · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Leuphasyl (pentapeptide-18) evidence consists of manufacturer studies only; no indexed human trial was found.
claims.reviewNote: no primary source exists — teach as 'no independent evidence', not as a mechanism · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Cosmetic peptides are regulated as cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is evaluated by a cosmetics framework rather than a drug-approval pathway.
claims.reviewNote: US framing; UK/EU cosmetics regulation to be added for the SEASON edition · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: BPC-157 evidence is an extensive rodent literature, largely from one research group; human data are uncontrolled case series; the first randomized human trials were registered in 2026 and have no results.
claims.reviewNote: guides rate C (A&RE) — Omar to confirm; two independent 2025–26 reviews now exist · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: TB-500 is the acetylated 17–23 fragment of thymosin β4 (Ac-LKKTETQ), not thymosin β4 itself; the fragment was characterized by analysing the product, and human trial data for the fragment do not exist.
claims.reviewNote: guide grade D · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: KPV, the C-terminal tripeptide of α-MSH, reduces inflammation in murine colitis models; no randomized human trials exist for any indication.
claims.reviewNote: guide grade C; the 'small open-label atopic dermatitis studies' the guide mentions could not be located on PubMed · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Topical LL-37 has two randomized placebo-controlled trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers: a small first-in-human dose-ranging trial (n=34) that was positive at low dose, and a larger phase IIb trial that was negative in its full cohort — a worked example of why a small positive trial is not confirmation.
claims.reviewNote: guide grade C; both trials authored by the developer · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: BPC-157, KPV and TB-500 (with MOTS-c, emideltide, semax and epitalon) were reviewed by FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee on July 23–24, 2026 for possible addition to the 503A bulks list; the committee's votes are advisory, FDA rulemaking is still required, and compounding these substances without bulks-list standing has drawn FDA warning letters.
claims.reviewNote: vote counts come from trade press, not FDA — cite them as unofficial or omit · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: Research-use-only peptide products are made outside GMP and carry documented risks of impurity, inaccurate dosing and heavy-metal contamination.
claims.reviewNote: A&RE asserts heavy-metal (arsenic, lead) contamination without a citation; no primary analytical study of skin-peptide RUO products was found. Adjacent evidence only. Either the author supplies the source or the lesson says 'reported, not documented'. · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

claims.text: GLOW (GHK-Cu + BPC-157 + TB-500) and KLOW (+ KPV) are marketing names for research-use-only blends with no controlled human trials.
claims.reviewNote: absence-of-evidence claim; the guides are sufficient · grader: Omar Saleem / Perceptors (grade column is theirs; the agent proposes a role and records the guide's rating only)

title.en: Cutaneous Neuro-Immuno-Endocrinology and Dermal Aging
